thread:
Sam: Aurora POC hold — legal wants BYOK (customer KMS) + EU procurement to sign order form before US exec signs MSA.

Priya: Paste their BYOK wording so legal can triage?

Sam: They pasted: "Customer shall provision and control cryptographic keys; Redwood will not have access to plaintext keys or key material."

Ravi: We can support BYOK only for Dedicated / Private deployments. Our hosted API cannot accept customer-managed keys today.

Mark: DocuSign two-envelope flow is blowing up for that signer sequence (EU-first then US). Template assumes single-envelope multi-signer.

Priya: Two-envelope is operationally acceptable, but we need an order-of-precedence clause so DPA data obligations stay bound. Draft: "Order of Precedence: the MSA controls, then the Order Form; the DPA governs data processing obligations and survives termination."

Ravi: About subprocessors — we provide a current list and will notify customers of material changes. We can't enumerate every infra provider contractually, but 30-day notice + right to object is standard.

Sam: They also want Net90 and PO up front for POC billing. Finance: how flexible?

billing-bot: billing-bot: Finance note: scanned/email PO accepted for POC invoicing. Standard terms Net30, exception to Net60 for pilot credit; Net90 requires exec approval.

Mark: I'll share a minimal private-VPC config for their security team:
```
deployment: private-vpc
kms: customer-managed-hsm
network: private-subnets + nat
logging: forward->s3+kinesis, retention: 90d
access: support via JIT tickets
```

Sam: Plan: send counter with (1) BYOK addendum limited to Dedicated/Private; (2) subproc notice language; (3) precedence clause; offer Net60 for POC and require exec signoff for Net90.

Priya: I'll assemble the redline and push to Aurora legal by EOD PST.

Ravi: Finance approves Net60 for the pilot. Escalate to VP if they insist on Net90.

Sam: Thanks all 139; sending now, will update when they reply. :thumbsup:
